Global capability centres

Building capabilities across borders

For a Japanese business, establishing a global capability centre in India is more than a location decision. It starts with deciding what the centre should contribute—and what capabilities, relationships and operating arrangements would make that possible.

The opportunity could involve technology, engineering, research, business operations or other specialist functions. The right approach depends on the business’s objectives, its readiness to work across borders and the responsibilities it wants to retain or share.

Questions worth exploring

  • What should the centre help the business achieve?
  • Which capabilities should it develop, and how should they connect with teams in Japan?
  • Should the business establish its own operation, work with a partner or develop the capability in stages?
  • What would it take to prepare the people, governance and working practices on both sides?

Where SetuHashi could contribute

  • Shape the opportunity

    Clarify the business need, assess possible approaches and develop the case for proceeding.

  • Connect the right participants

    Identify and assess potential operating, technology, talent and specialist partners against the agreed requirements.

  • Prepare for delivery

    Help define responsibilities, governance and a staged implementation plan, and coordinate participants as the assignment requires.

A practical starting point

An assessment of the intended capability, possible operating approaches and the decisions needed before committing to a setup plan.
